content.title: Big Investors Clap Back Against Private Funds for Individuals
content.summary: Private equity’s push to sell funds to individual investors is triggering a backlash from institutions such as pensions and insurers that have owned such funds for decades.  The Institutional Limited Partners Association, an industry group for institutions that invest in private funds, is sounding the alarm bell about the trend, calling it “inevitable” and a potential conflict of interest for fund managers.  “There are questions about the timing of investments (including initial and follow-on) and exits, as well as overall portfolio construction, and whether Investment Advisers will optimize outcomes for retail investors at the expense of institutional investors,” ILPA said Tuesday in a white paper.
